title: Interceptive Billing Normalizer for Per-route Metering
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Build a lightweight normalization service ("Interceptive Billing Normalizer") that runs as a streaming job between ingestion and billing-aggregation to: 1) deduplicate and reconcile interleaved events across billing windows, 2) apply per-route normalization rules (e.g., remove internal pings, apply sampling adjustments, unify model-variant identifiers), and 3) emit idempotent, ledger-ready records to billing-ready topics.

Goals:
- Ensure billing-ready topic contains one canonical usage record per customer-request-id per logical route per billing-window.
- Handle late-arriving and out-of-order tokens with two-phase reconciliation (fast path + scheduled backfill).
- Provide a compact fingerprinting scheme to detect semantic duplicates across model aliases and minor prompt rewrites.
- Support retroactive corrections without creating double-billing by using correction markers and tombstones.

Design notes:
- Input: raw-events Kafka topic (schema v2) with fields (request_id, customer_id, route, model_id, timestamp, token_counts, delta_flags, metadata).
- Normalizer logic: compute "usage_fingerprint" based on stable fields (customer_id, route, canonical_model, prefix_hash). Keep a per-window state store keyed by (customer_id, window_id, usage_fingerprint) storing best record and last_seen timestamp.
- Outputs: billing-ready topic (canonical records) and billing-audit topic (rejected/merged inputs for debugging). Emit tombstone messages when a previous canonical record is replaced.
- Backpressure/throughput: target 10k events/s per partition with 99th pct processing latency < 200ms on our dedicated cluster.
- Idempotency: include canonical_record_id and source_event_ids array capped to N to allow audit without unbounded growth.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Start in shadow mode for one low-traffic org (2 weeks).
2) Enable as soft-write for experimental customers; create reconciliation dashboard in Console.
3) Full write path for small orgs; monitor refund rate and billing diffs.
4) Gradual rollout to all tenants with two-week monitoring windows and automatic rollback on >0.5% unexpected charge delta.

Operational considerations:
- Provide a tool to replay ranges from raw-events to rehydrate state store.
- Retention: keep state for 60 days to support corrections and audits.
- Security: ensure PII fields are redacted before logs; integrate with existing KMS for any exported audit bundles.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test demonstrating duplicate suppression for synthetic interleaved events.
- Billing diffs for shadow org < 0.1% after 2 weeks.
- Console dashboard with per-route reconciliation rate and late-arriving event histogram.
